valuation.method: Forward non-GAAP EPS x justified P/E at the 12-month target date (about 2027-11-18). At that date the forward twelve months are mostly fiscal 2028 (year ending January 2028). FY2027 (year ending 31 January 2027) non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance is $1.25 to $1.26 (midpoint $1.255) from the Q2 FY2027 release of 26 August 2026, with a 21.0% non-GAAP tax rate. The scenario EPS values for FY2028 are model assumptions, not company guidance: bear $1.40, base $1.60, bull $1.80. Non-GAAP EPS excludes stock-based compensation; GAAP net income for Q2 FY2027 was only $5.3 million. Listing is USD on NASDAQ, so no FX conversion applies and targets are per share of the same listing.

bear.driver: Growth decelerates after the FY2027 net new ARR peak and the multiple compresses as the stock is priced for perfection

base.driver: Revenue growth near the mid-20s percent holds with operating leverage; non-GAAP EPS compounds from the FY2027 midpoint

bull.driver: Net new ARR keeps accelerating on AI security demand and the market keeps a premium multiple for the growth

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $1.60 the close of $226.61 implies 142x; on FY2027 guidance midpoint $1.255 it implies 181x. The Street-weighted target of about $250 (aggregator mean, 50 analysts) implies 156x base EPS, or $1.67 EPS at 150x (about 4% above the base EPS).
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $1.60 (0.7 pp of the close). A $0.10 change in FY2028 EPS moves it by $15.00 (6.6 pp of the close).
valuation.watch_metric: Net new ARR and the FY2027 non-GAAP EPS path: the Q2 net new ARR of $332.8 million and the raised net new ARR growth outlook must keep compounding for EPS to reach $1.60 in FY2028
valuation.next_disclosure: Q3 FY2027 results, expected around 1 to 2 December 2026 (aggregator date 2026-12-01 is not confirmed by the company)

analyst_notes: Named views dated before the reference close are sparse: only four analysts (Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy with a $300 target from $240 on 2 November 2026; Jefferies raised to $240 from $230 after Q2; Goldman Sachs kept Buy at $230; Bernstein kept Hold and lifted to $177 from $132 on 9 November). Most post-Q2 targets sit in a $230 to $310 band, and the aggregator mean of about $250 is above our $240 base, a gap of roughly 4% in target, or about $0.07 of FY2028 EPS at 150x. Calls dated 13 November or later (for example Morgan Stanley $254, Rosenblatt $275, Wells Fargo $300, TD Cowen $280) are after the reference close and are excluded from the events list and the weighted target; the unnamed firm-level figures in the 6 November roundup (UBS $310, Citigroup $295, Bank of America Hold $290, Mizuho $275) have no analyst names and are not counted.
